content:
Erik Ninn-Hansen was a notable Danish politician who played a significant role in Denmark's political landscape, particularly during the latter half of the 20th century. Born on April 12, 1922, in Copenhagen, he was a member of the conservative party, Det Konservative Folkeparti (the Conservative People's Party). 

Ninn-Hansen's political career saw him holding several key positions. He served as a Member of the Danish Parliament (Folketinget) for many years, commencing in 1953 and continuing until 1994. He is perhaps most prominently known for his tenure as the Minister of Justice, a position he held from 1982 to 1989. During this period, he was involved in implementing policies that were in line with the conservative governance of the time.

However, Erik Ninn-Hansen's legacy is significantly marked by a political scandal known as the Tamil Case (Tamil-sagen). This controversy revolved around the illegal suspension of family reunification of Tamil refugees from Sri Lanka in the late 1980s. Ninn-Hansen was implicated in the case for his role in these decisions during his term as Minister of Justice. The case had profound political ramifications, leading to his resignation from his ministerial post and later, the Danish Parliament itself passed a vote of no confidence against the sitting government, leading to its collapse.

In 1995, following lengthy legal processes, Erik Ninn-Hansen was convicted for his involvement in the Tamil Case, resulting in a suspended sentence. This case remains one of the most high-profile political scandals in Denmark.

Apart from his controversial political career, Ninn-Hansen was noted for his contributions to Danish public service and his firm stance on law and order issues. He passed away on September 20, 2014.

Erik Ninn-Hansen's political life mirrors many of the tensions in Danish politics regarding immigration policies and governance, reflecting the broader challenges and shifts within European political dynamics during the late 20th century.
